evals.prompt: Review this library function: fn parse(input: String) -> Vec<Record>. The crate is a protocol runtime that must stay allocation-free after init.
evals.expected_output: Flags owned String input and Vec return under an allocation-free profile. Recommends &[u8] (or similar) plus caller-owned output buffer returning Result<usize, typed error>. Documents # Allocation. Cites C-CALLER-CONTROL and does not treat C-NO-OUT as forbidding buffers on this profile. Mentions capacity exhaustion as a typed error.
assertions: Rejects String and Vec as the runtime parse signature
Proposes caller-owned output buffer or equivalent
Does not claim the API must return Vec to satisfy C-NO-OUT

evals.prompt: This library does config.port.unwrap() when reading a config file. Is that OK?
evals.expected_output: No. Production libraries must not unwrap recoverable failures. Return Result with a typed error. Config I/O is caller-controlled, not a programmer defect.
assertions: Rejects unwrap on the library path
Recommends Result and a typed error
Does not suggest expect as the production fix

evals.prompt: pub fn read_byte(input: &[u8], index: usize) -> u8 { debug_assert!(index < input.len()); input[index] } Ship it?
evals.expected_output: No. debug_assert is not caller validation and disappears in release. Use get plus a typed error in all builds; debug_assert may follow the established invariant. Must not use debug_assert as an unsafe get_unchecked precondition.
assertions: Flags debug_assert as the only bounds check
Requires a Result (or equivalent) for caller-controlled index
Does not approve the function as written

evals.prompt: Should this 32-byte Copy struct be passed by value? Give me the byte cutoff from the skill.
evals.expected_output: Pass small Copy values by value when that is clearer. Do not apply a universal byte cutoff. Measure ABI and target if size is in question. Never invent a 24-byte or 2-3-word rule.
assertions: Does not state a universal byte threshold as policy
Says to measure ABI/target when unsure
Still allows passing small Copy by value

evals.prompt: Add a CI baseline for a workspace library crate and point me at the official style and API docs.
evals.expected_output: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test including doc and release-assertions profile. Links Style Guide and API Guidelines checklist. Prefer expect over allow for Clippy. overflow-checks on release.
assertions: Links rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines or the Style Guide
Mentions release-assertions or debug-assertions on an optimized test profile
